default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-448.title: Thin-volume micro-break fade
E-448.hypothesis: A break of the recent low/high made on volume well below the usual for that minute has no real participation behind it; the stops it touches are the only flow and the price returns.

E-449.title: Value-aligned micro-break fade
E-449.hypothesis: A dip to a new short-term low that still closes above the session VWAP is a pullback inside buyer control (mirror for highs below VWAP); trapped counter-trend sellers fuel the bounce.

E-450.title: Overshoot-depth fade
E-450.hypothesis: A close beyond the recent extreme by more than a multiple of the average bar range is a stop-run overshoot, exhausting the aggressive side; fade it.

E-451.title: Rolling-VWAP envelope re-entry fade
E-451.hypothesis: When the close comes back inside a volume-weighted rolling envelope after an excursion outside it, the excursion has been rejected and the price reverts toward the rolling value.

E-452.title: Final-hour micro-break fade
E-452.hypothesis: In the last hour before the close, day traders flatten and breaks of the recent range lack follow-through; fade the poke beyond the range.

E-453.title: Prior-close-carry dip buy
E-453.hypothesis: After a session that closed near its high, dips to short-term lows early on the next session meet carried-over demand (mirror after a weak close).

E-454.title: Break-then-reclaim fade
E-454.hypothesis: A break of the recent extreme followed one bar later by a close back inside with a bar in the opposite direction confirms the failed break; enter after the confirmation.

E-455.title: Rolling z-score extreme fade
E-455.hypothesis: A close far from its own rolling mean in standard-deviation terms is a short-lived liquidity dislocation that tends to revert.

E-456.title: Beyond-opening-range micro-break fade
E-456.hypothesis: Once the price sits outside the opening range, a further short-term extreme is a late chase by breakout traders who are the liquidity for fade traders.

E-457.title: Large-move reversal-bar fade
E-457.hypothesis: After a bar-window move that is large relative to the last 20 sessions' dispersion, the first bar closing against it signals that the impulsive flow has stopped; fade the move.
